Carlos — thanks, and great questions. Below is a concise summary for inclusion in your RFP; I've attached a short spec (auditline_spec_v1.pdf) and an NDJSON sample. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through.

Key points (summary):
- Sampling protocol: supports deterministic time-window slicing, event-type filters, and pseudo-random sampling using a seed tied to request id. For sampling fidelity we surface sampling rates (e.g., 1%, 5%, 10%) and can provide confidence intervals. For critical event classes (auth, iam-change, export) we recommend no sampling; full fidelity is the default for those types.
- Lead times: ad-hoc slice (<= 30 days): typical delivery 48–72 business hours. Historical bulk (>= 12 months): depends on data volume — typical SLA 7–14 business days for a full tenant export; we provide an ETA during request intake and support expedited paths for contracted accounts.
- Formats & packaging: NDJSON and Parquet supported. Exports are gzipped by default (.ndjson.gz / .parquet.gz). Each export bundle includes a machine-readable manifest (JSON) with byte offsets, record counts, per-file SHA256 checksums, and a top-level SHA256 for the bundle.
- Transfer methods: we support S3-to-S3 (customer bucket, cross-account role or presigned PUT), direct HTTPS pull with time-limited signed URLs, and SFTP for customers that require it. We can perform server-side encryption with your KMS or our managed KMS.
- Tamper-evidence & timestamping: manifests are signed with a Redwood-managed certificate (X.509) and we can provide an optional timestamp token from an RFC 3161 time-stamping authority. For high-assurance legal holds we offer a signed chain-of-custody report (see attached spec section 4.2).
- Redaction & PII: exports can be delivered raw, or with configurable redaction rules (field-level or regex-based). Redaction is applied at export time; we include a redaction log describing transformations. Note: redaction may remove cryptographic reproducibility for those records.

Attachments: auditline_spec_v1.pdf (spec + manifest samples), sample_ndjson_export_sample.ndjson (sliced sample).

Next steps: if you need per-request tamper-evidence (detached signature + RFC3161 timestamp), please indicate in the RFP. Ben and Laura are looped in for pricing & security attestations.

Hi Jill / Carlos — I wanted to add a few technical assurances and practical steps we follow for forensic-grade exports: 

- Sampling variance example: for an event class with N events = 100,000 over 30 days, a 5% simple random sample (n = 5,000) has an approximate standard error sqrt(p(1-p)/n) -> ~0.0043; 95% CI for proportion estimates is +/- 0.85 percentage points. We include a short CSV in the spec with a few worked examples (see auditline_spec_v1.pdf, appendix B).
- Signed manifests & verification: our manifests are signed with an RSA-2048 key; we can publish the public cert fingerprint and provide a verification command using openssl to validate the detached signature against the manifest and to verify RFC3161 timestamps. Example verification steps are in section 4.3 of the attached spec.
- Legal hold & incremental exports: we support tenant-level preservation flags that suspend scheduled deletion and produce incremental exports filtered by timestamp > hold_date. Incremental exports include a delta manifest highlighting new records and a rolling chain-of-custody.
- Chain-of-custody artifacts: for legal holds we generate a PDF chain-of-custody report that lists delivery handoffs, cryptographic hashes, and the timestamp authority token. We retain a copy of the signed manifest for the contracted retention period.

I'll be on the call if you'd like to walk through the verification steps. Proposed next step: 30-minute technical walkthrough next week to review the verification command, and for Ben to present the proposed pricing envelope.

Regards,
